question: An operations manager is worried that letting a long negotiation chat condense itself will destroy the record of what was said. Which statement is accurate?
options: A) Earlier messages are condensed so the chat can continue, and the full chat history stays readable to her.
B) Earlier messages are moved into project knowledge automatically, where colleagues can then also read them.
C) Earlier messages are stripped out of the chat entirely, so only the condensed version can be reviewed.
D) Earlier messages are exported to a file on her account, which she must download before the chat resumes.
correct_answers: A) Earlier messages are condensed so the chat can continue, and the full chat history stays readable to her.
explanations: Correct. Automatic context management compresses what is held in working memory to make room, while the complete history remains accessible in the conversation.
Incorrect. Condensed content is not exported into a project, and nothing is shared with colleagues as a side effect.
Incorrect. Nothing is removed from the history. Compression affects working memory rather than the stored conversation.
Incorrect. There is no download step; the conversation continues without any manual action from her.
